chunk_findings.detail: Given an environment where the built-in module `ddflow.services.lane_headless` cannot be imported (for example, an optional dependency it pulls in is missing, or a partial install lacks the module), `driver_for("process-headless")` calls `importlib.import_module("ddflow.services.lane_headless")` and lets the resulting `ImportError` propagate. The function is annotated `Lane | Result` and documented as returning an `unavailable` Result when it cannot provide the transport, and the stated intent is that a missing capability is reported unavailable; instead the caller crashes with an exception.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lane_driver.py:driver_for

chunk_findings.detail: If an optional string parameter is `None` instead of the empty string—common when a config field has no value—`spec_from_headless` treats it as a real value. For example, with a descriptor whose `model_flag` is `"--model"`, `spec_from_headless("lane", headless, model=None)` passes the `val != ""` test, stores `values["model"] = str(None) == "None"`, and appends `--model {model}`; the lane is launched with the literal model name `None` rather than leaving the model unset. The same happens for `effort`, `mcp_config`, and `session`; a `session=None` with a resume flag becomes a resume session id of `"None"`, guessing a value instead of reporting absence.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lane_driver.py:spec_from_headless

chunk_findings.detail: The child environment is built by setting `HOME` (and `home_env`) to the lane-private home and then applying `spec.fixed_env` and `r.env` afterwards. Given `LaunchSpec(fixed_env={"HOME": "[REDACTED:path]"})`, or a rendered `r.env` containing `HOME`, the final child `HOME` is the non-private value, not the lane-private directory. The driver then removes only the private directory it created, so the agent can read/write config under the user’s real home and the cleanup/isolation contract is broken.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lane_headless.py:_prepare

chunk_findings.detail: Prompt delivery is keyed on the wrong signal: `_prepare` only writes `prompt.txt` when `"{prompt_file}"` is an exact argv element, while `start` later decides whether to write stdin based on `"prompt_file" in values`. If a caller supplies `spec.values={"prompt_file": "/tmp/stale"}` while using `spec.argv=["agent"]` and `spec.prompt="secret"`, `_prepare` never creates the prompt file, but `start` sees `prompt_file` in `values`, skips the stdin writer, and closes stdin. The prompt is silently dropped. The same proxy also fails for templates that embed the placeholder inside an argv token, e.g. `--prompt-file={prompt_file}`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lane_headless.py:_prepare/start

chunk_findings.detail: When `spec.home` is supplied, `_prepare` may create `prompt.txt` inside that directory, but the directory is not added to `private`, and `_cleanup` only removes `private`. For example, with `spec.home=Path("/tmp/lane-home")`, `spec.argv=["agent", "{prompt_file}"]`, and `spec.prompt="secret"`, the driver writes `/tmp/lane-home/prompt.txt`; after `stop()` or a post-exit `status()`, that prompt file remains. The driver-created prompt is not cleaned up even when the launch later fails before spawn.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lane_headless.py:_prepare/_cleanup

chunk_findings.detail: `status()` calls `_cleanup()` as soon as the leader process has an exit code, without stopping the process group. If the headless agent forks a background worker in the same process group and then exits, `status()` sees the leader exit and removes the lane-private home while the worker is still running. On Unix this deletes the home directory out from under the surviving process, violating the stated cleanup-by-process-group behavior and causing later file creation or agent state writes to fail.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lane_headless.py:status

chunk_findings.detail: `--echo-env` and `--pwd-home` construct JSON with `%` interpolation instead of `json.dumps`, so environment values containing `"` or `\` (or control characters) emit invalid JSON. For example, with `HOME=C:\Users\test` on Windows, `--pwd-home` prints `{"type":"home","home":"C:\Users\test"}`; the backslashes are invalid JSON escapes, so a driver parsing stdout treats the line as noise and the lane-private home telemetry assertion fails. The same occurs on any platform with an env value containing a double quote.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/lane_driver/fake_agent.py:38

chunk_findings.detail: The test waits only for `pidfile.exists()` and then immediately does `child = int(pidfile.read_text())`. File existence does not guarantee that the file contains a complete PID. If `fake_agent.py` writes the child PID with the usual non-atomic `open(..., "w")` / `Path.write_text(...)` sequence, the test can observe the file after truncation but before the full write, or after a partial write. For example, if the real child PID is `12345` and the test reads `12`, it then waits for PID `12` (often an unrelated long-lived process) and fails with “the grandchild outlived the group kill”; if it reads an empty file, `int()` raises `ValueError`. This makes the test intermittently fail even when the driver correctly killed the process group.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_driver.py:test_stop_kills_the_whole_process_group_and_removes_home

chunk_findings.detail: The test named `..._writes_a_private_file` never inspects the prompt file: it only asserts that `start` did not return a `Result` and that the lane finishes. If the driver writes a prompt file with the wrong content, with permissive permissions such as `0644`, or fails to clean it up, the test still passes. It can therefore pass while violating the “private file” contract the test is supposed to enforce.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_driver.py:test_prompt_file_placeholder_writes_a_private_file

chunk_findings.detail: The `scope` knob declares `strictest=("none", "the process group alone, which needs nothing installed")`, but the same knob’s `doc` identifies `"systemd"` as the stricter option because it adds an extra cgroup and `"none"` as only the process group. If any policy or tool consumes `strictest` to request the most restrictive scope, it will select the weaker process-group-only containment even when `systemd` is available, contradicting the knob’s own semantics and the change’s containment intent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/lanes.py:53

chunk_findings.detail: The placeholder check happens after the flag check, so a headless template that already contains a placeholder is still rejected when the corresponding flag is empty. For example, with `headless.argv = ("agent", "{model}")`, `headless.model_flag = ""`, and `model = "gpt-5"`, the code returns `unavailable("the descriptor has no flag for model; it is not guessed")` even though no flag is needed because the template already carries `"{model}"`. The function's own contract says the flag is added only when the template does not already carry that placeholder.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lane_driver.py:spec_from_headless

chunk_findings.detail: The `--child` branch starts the grandchild with `subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", "import time;time.sleep(300)"])` without redirecting its stdout/stderr, so the long-lived grandchild inherits the fake agent's stdout/stderr pipe write ends. If the fake agent is launched with `stdout=PIPE` (for example `subprocess.run([sys.executable, "fake_agent.py", "ok.jsonl", "--child", pid], stdout=PIPE, timeout=5)`), the direct fake agent exits immediately after replay, but the pipe write end remains open for 300 seconds; a caller reading stdout to EOF blocks until that sleep ends instead of seeing EOF when the fake agent itself has exited. The child should be started with stdout/stderr `DEVNULL` or otherwise detached from the parent's pipes.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/lane_driver/fake_agent.py:31

chunk_findings.detail: The `spec` helper calls `ld.LaunchSpec(name="t", argv=argv, stream_rules=RULES, limit=LIMIT, stop_grace_s=2, **kw)`. Because `stop_grace_s` is passed explicitly before `**kw`, any caller that puts `stop_grace_s` in the helper’s extra kwargs (e.g. `spec(stop_grace_s=1)`) makes the call raise `TypeError: got multiple values for keyword argument 'stop_grace_s'`, so the helper cannot override this supported `LaunchSpec` option.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_driver.py:spec

data.summary: Every `ddflow heartbeat` of DRV-lane-interface printed "YIELD REQUESTED: fix-Be927e56fb6 waits for the files DRV-lane-interface holds", yet fix-Be927e56fb6 (globs ddflow/api/jobs.py, ddflow/api/review.py, ddflow/surfaces/*/review.py, tests/test_review_*.py) shares no file with DRV-lane-interface's globs and is itself leased by kilo-driver. Repeated for 30 min. Compare `ddflow show` of both.
data.title: False YIELD REQUESTED on heartbeat: waiter's globs do not overlap the holder's

data.body:
Fixes bug B38ebc3e392: Every `ddflow heartbeat` of DRV-lane-interface printed "YIELD REQUESTED: fix-Be927e56fb6 waits for the files DRV-lane-interface holds", yet fix-Be927e56fb6 (globs ddflow/api/jobs.py, ddflow/api/review.py, ddflow/surfaces/*/review.py, tests/test_review_*.py) shares no file with DRV-lane-interface's globs and is itself leased by kilo-driver. Repeated for 30 min. Compare `ddflow show` of both. Found on DRV-lane-interface.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B38ebc3e392 --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B38ebc3e392 --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug B38ebc3e392: False YIELD REQUESTED on heartbeat: waiter's globs do not overlap the holder's
